results.title: Ghanaians hold on to cherished food traditions as Christmas approaches
results.content: As Christmas approaches, families are preparing to celebrate the festive season with meals that bring them together and keep cherished food traditions alive. For many households, Christmas is not just about the celebrations but also the special dishes that have become part of their family traditions. Yet, with the cost of food and festive preparations often a concern, some families are finding ways to maintain their favourite meals without giving up what makes the season special. Speaking in a Christmas series exploring the foods families cannot do without during the festive season, Daniel Thompson said his family would continue preparing eba, describing it as an affordable meal. He said the family might switch from yellow gari to white gari to manage costs, but eba would remain part of their Christmas menu.

results.title: Ayariga urges residents to keep surroundings clean as AMA deploys 20 tricycles
results.content: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has urged residents to take greater responsibility for sanitation by ensuring waste is properly disposed of rather than leaving refuse outside their homes for government authorities to collect. He said keeping communities clean should go beyond maintaining individual homes to include the surrounding environment, stressing that sanitation was a shared responsibility. “Sometimes people clean their home and just put the waste right in front, and then they make it the responsibility of government to come and take the waste right in front of their homes,” he said.

results.title: Afua Kobi Ampem SHS wins Ashanti NHIS inter-school quiz
results.content: Afua Kobi Ampem Senior High School has emerged winner of the Ashanti Regional edition of the National Health Insurance Authority’s (NHIA) inter-school quiz competition, beating Ibadur Rahman Academy SHS and Opoku Ware School. The competition forms part of a nationwide public education initiative aimed at improving students’ understanding of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), including its benefits, entitlements and operations. Organised under the auspices of NHIA Chief Executive, Dr Victor Asare Bampoe, the initiative involves 48 schools across the country. Participating schools were provided with study materials and sensitisation to strengthen their knowledge of the scheme ahead of the regional contests.

results.title: GH¢31bn informal cross-border trade faces hurdles despite AfCFTA commitments
results.content: Informal cross-border trade in Ghana, estimated at GH¢31 billion in the first three quarters of 2025, continues to face significant operational challenges, raising concerns about the country's ability to fully harness the benefits of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

results.title: Cross-border traders allege harassment, illegal levies without formal complaint channels

results.title: EU-funded study finds heavy metal contamination in Savannah mining communities
results.content: An EU-funded study has found elevated levels of heavy metals in soil samples from artisanal and small-scale mining communities in three districts of the Savannah Region, raising concerns about environmental contamination and potential health risks. The baseline studies, conducted under the European Union-funded Gold for Good (G4G) Project, found that cadmium levels exceeded recommended guidelines in all soil samples collected, while mercury concentrations were above recommended limits in about 94 per cent of the samples. The findings also point to significant gaps in mining regulation and oversight, with only 2.92 per cent of respondents holding mining licences and approximately 74 per cent unaware of the regulations governing mining activities in their communities.

results.title: Ntiamoah Foundation marks 20 years of impact with community outreach, donations and stakeholder engagement
results.content: New Abirem, Eastern Region, 27 October 2026: Ntiamoah Foundation has marked its 20th anniversary with two days of community engagement, project monitoring, health screening and donations to schools and healthcare facilities in the Birim North and South Districts of the Eastern Region.
